measurement.gap_nodes: 40000 - sum(cell.volume) over all living cells at that logged time
measurement.closure_call: an arm is CLOSED when gap_nodes reaches 0 before t_end, otherwise ARRESTED
measurement.trajectories: cell.center.x, cell.center.y per cell per logged time
measurement.mechanical_cost: interface energy J*sum(cell.surface touching medium) is NOT separable from the logged total surface, so the reported cost is the volume-constraint term lambda_V * sum((cell.volume - 625)^2) plus lambda_S * the logged aspherity term; both are CPM energy in model units and neither is a force or a stress.

gates.name: held-out: threshold scales with interface energy
gates.statement: Revision 1 bracketed the k=4 closure threshold at lambda_V in (0.3, 1.0) with J=140. Phi is linear in lambda_V and inverse in J, so at J=280 the threshold must sit in (0.6, 2.0). The measured J=280 bracket's geometric-mean threshold must fall in that interval.
gates.why: the prediction comes from the algebraic form of Phi and revision 1's J=140 bracket. No J=280 result is used to derive it, so this is a genuine out-of-sample test of the group's J-dependence. It tests only that dependence; revision 1 already refuted a constant Phi* across gap size, and G9 does not re-open that.

gates.name: no-drive control does not close
gates.statement: F1-no-drive-NEGATIVE ends with gap >= 0.95 * its initial gap.
gates.why: replaces revision 1's G4, which turned off only one of the two drives. If the gap closes with both off, closure is an artifact of the volume constraint or the initialisation, not of either modelled mechanism.

gates.name: protrusion dose-response is monotone
gates.statement: At k=4 and lambda_V=1, closed_fraction is non-decreasing in protrusion strength over {0, 20, 40, 80, 160}; the 80 point is revision 1's B-k4-lamV1.
gates.why: Bai & Zeng 2023 report that promoting lamellipodial protrusion raises the closure rate, over an assumed 0.2-10 pN range in a finite-element model. This checks whether this CPM carries the same ordering. Agreement is between two models and is not experimental validation; a CPM protrusion strength is not a force in piconewtons.

gates.name: gap ladder is complete
gates.statement: A closure threshold bracket exists at k=1, 4 and 7, and the three fitted Phi* values are reported together with whether they agree.
gates.bound: reported; a constant Phi* is NOT asserted
gates.why: revision 1 found Phi* rising as the gap shrinks. This records the full ladder so the domain of any rule is stated from three points rather than two.

supersedes: artifacts/epithelial/protocol.json (revision 1). Revision 1's arms and gate outcomes stand as run; no revision 1 bound is changed and no revision 1 failure is relabelled.
not_claimed: This is not a reproduction of Bai & Zeng 2023. Their mechanics is 3D continuum finite element with cohesive-zone traction-separation laws; a Cellular Potts Model implements none of those equations. Only the geometric construction is shared: Voronoi monolayer, wound by removing central cells, no proliferation.
No parameter here is calibrated to any cell line, species or measured tissue. CPM energies are in model units inherited from the upstream Act-model example.
Closure times in model time units are not minutes, hours or any measured closure rate.
No purse-string actomyosin cable is modelled. Closure here is interface energy plus Act-model protrusion only.
Agreement between this model's behaviour and a published trend is model-level agreement. It is not experimental validation and does not raise the evidence level of either.
